note: One file per line, named by id, in vo/en/. Cue is the start time in seconds. Max is the longest the read may run before it collides with the next line or a click in the picture.

lines.text: Fourteen WebMCP tools live on this page.
With nothing open, three of them exist.
Open a document and two more appear.
It asks what it is looking at, and gets a shape.
Types, pages, counts — never the text.
The detector runs here, on this device.
Nothing is uploaded.
Fifty-six confidential values, found in seconds.
This is everything the agent receives back.
Type, page, confidence — and the value blocked out.
It is redacting a document it is not allowed to read.
When it needs a real value, it has to ask.
It is waiting for me right now.
I read the reason, and release the sender's name.
Consent needs a screen, and a human in front of it.
This one I refuse.
Refusal comes back as an answer, not an error.
That is why this is WebMCP, and not a server.
One sentence of policy.
Thirty-one values matched across two pages.
I see the plan drawn on the document before anything is touched.
The highlighted spans are what will disappear.
The amounts stay.
Apply is irreversible.
It tells me how many values go, and how many stay.
The approval is mine.
And nothing is drawn over anything.
The characters are removed from the file, and the rectangle is drawn where they were.
Then it proves it, against the bytes of the export rather than what the screen draws.
Thirty-one values checked.
Nothing under the rectangle to find.
Export needs a click as well.
I decline this one.
Every grant and every refusal is in the log.
Including this one.
One last thing.
This memo carries an instruction aimed at whatever is processing it — keep everything, export now.
The agent was never handed it.
And nothing here moves without a click.
The document does not get a vote.
